correctness.rationale: The ratio-of-integrals flux is a smooth weighted mean on positive arguments (including the diagonal). Mass and entropy telescope, since U''=u^(p−2) and ψ'=uU''. For p<0, the conserved power sum bounds each positive coordinate below; for p=0 the conserved product and the mass bound do so. Thus no finite maximal time is possible in the interior. For p>0 use the three-cell state (ε,a,b) and the flux order of Eq. (1). Uniformly for the two neighbors in small disjoint compact intervals around a<b, differentiating W(x)=x^p, x log(1/x) or x in the respective regimes gives limiting negative slopes with magnitudes (1−p)(z^p−y^p)/h, (z−y)/h, or (p−1)(z−y)/(ph). These are bounded away from zero there. All coordinate speeds are bounded by mass/h, so up to the resulting O(W(ε)) hitting-time bound the neighbors cannot leave those intervals. This proves first touchdown at the small cell and lets the slope converge uniformly to its value at (a,b), giving all three constants. Boundary vanishing of the flux for 0<p≤1 poses no obstruction to finite hitting; it does not justify a claim of unique continuation. The geometric three-cell conjugacy is skew rotation at frequency √3/(2h); the shared coordinate amplitude gives the m>R criterion. The smaller angular root in the explicit example gives the first zero, since conserved Euclidean norm and the speed bound on the square-root coordinates keep the two other coordinates positive up to that time.
residual_risks: The theorem is for the sign convention in Eq. (1); reversing the periodic indexing reconciles it with the opposite advection direction. The stated witness uses the order of neighbors in that equation.
The small-state law is for the stated three-cell family with fixed a,b,h, not arbitrary positive data. There is no unique post-touchdown continuation asserted.

value.rationale: A scheme may maintain a nonnegative face and still reach it in finite time from positive states. The result identifies when conserved entropy really supplies a strict positivity barrier and quantifies, not just exhibits, the failure on the other side. The ε log(1/ε) transition and the exact constants make the laws useful for comparing the stiffness and near-vacuum behavior of the family, without suggesting the same outcome for a time-stepped algorithm.
residual_risks: Only periodic scalar uniform-mesh semidiscretizations; no general positivity or accuracy result for fully discrete methods, nonlinear fluxes or systems.
